subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should the remaining fix path prioritize a shared scheme-aware SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy repair, or should this be treated as part of the broader Telegram DNS/IPv4 transport policy work?
rationale: Current source and Undici contract evidence make the SOCKS proxy gap plausible, but choosing the permanent behavior affects shared proxy compatibility and overlaps with unmerged Telegram network-policy PRs.

options.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
options.body: Land or replace the proxy helper change so explicit and environment SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS routes behave consistently, then require focused tests and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Fold Into DNS/IPv4 Policy Work
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader Telegram transport-policy cluster and keep the issue open until the IPv4/DNS direction is accepted and proven.

options.title: Wait For Fresh Reporter Proof
options.body: Ask for current-release service-context logs before prioritizing a code path, accepting that the open candidate PR remains blocked meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
recommendation.body: Land or replace the proxy helper change so explicit and environment SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS routes behave consistently, then require focused tests and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about Telegram transport behavior, and obviyus is the strongest Telegram subsystem and fallback-chain history signal.
